uz.earliestSettlement: Samarkand is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in Central Asia, settled by at least the 7th century BC.

keyDates.event: Alexander the Great conquers Sogdiana, including Samarkand
Timur (Tamerlane) makes Samarkand the capital of his empire
Russian Empire captures Tashkent
Uzbek SSR formed within the Soviet Union
Independence from the Soviet Union, September 1
Shavkat Mirziyoyev becomes president, launching a reform era

uz.climate: Mostly arid continental desert/steppe, hot summers and cold winters.
funFacts: Tashkent's metro, opened in 1977, was the first in Central Asia - and its stations are famous for lavish, palace-like decoration.
Samarkand's Registan Square has stood as a public square for roughly 600 years.
Uzbekistan is one of only two 'doubly landlocked' countries in the world (the other is Liechtenstein) - meaning it's landlocked by other landlocked countries.
The Silk Road ran directly through Uzbekistan, making Bukhara and Samarkand major trading hubs for over a thousand years.
Plov has regional variants across the country - Samarkand's version differs from Tashkent's and Fergana's.

kz.earliestSettlement: The Botai culture, in northern Kazakhstan, is associated with some of the earliest evidence of horse domestication, around 3500 BC.

keyDates.event: Kazakh Khanate founded
Beginning of Russian imperial expansion into Kazakh lands
Kazakh SSR established
Independence from the Soviet Union, December 16
Capital moved from Almaty to Akmola, soon renamed Astana
Astana renamed Nur-Sultan, then reverted to Astana in 2022

kz.climate: Continental, with hot summers and very cold winters; semi-arid to arid in the south.

unesco.name: Saryarka – Steppe and Lakes of Northern Kazakhstan

funFacts: Kazakhstan is the world's largest landlocked country by area.
The Baikonur Cosmodrome, leased to Russia, is the world's first and largest operational space launch facility - it's where Yuri Gagarin launched into orbit.
Kazakhstan is believed to be where horses were first domesticated, roughly 5,500 years ago.
Almaty means 'father of apples' - the wild ancestor of the domestic apple, Malus sieversii, originated in the mountains near the city.
Kazakhstan voluntarily gave up the world's fourth-largest nuclear arsenal after independence in the 1990s.

tj.earliestSettlement: Sarazm, a proto-urban settlement near Panjakent, dates back to around 4000 BC.

keyDates.event: Tajik SSR separated from the Uzbek SSR
Independence from the Soviet Union, September 9
Civil war begins, lasting until 1997
Peace agreement ends the Tajik Civil War

tj.climate: Continental, strongly varied by elevation - hot lowlands, alpine Pamir highlands.

unesco.name: Tajik National Park (Mountains of the Pamirs)

funFacts: The Nurek Dam was, for decades, the tallest dam in the world.
Over 90% of Tajikistan is mountainous, most of it part of the Pamir and Alay ranges.
The Pamirs are nicknamed the 'Roof of the World'.
Tajik is a form of Persian, making Tajikistan the only Persian-speaking country in Central Asia.

kg.earliestSettlement: The Sulaiman-Too mountain in Osh has been a place of worship and settlement for over 3,000 years.

keyDates.event: Kirghiz SSR established
Independence from the Soviet Union, August 31
Tulip Revolution ousts President Akayev
Second revolution leads to a parliamentary system of government

kg.climate: Continental and strongly mountainous, with sharp altitude-driven variation.
funFacts: Lake Issyk-Kul is the second-largest alpine lake in the world after Titicaca, and it never freezes despite the surrounding snow.
The Epic of Manas, Kyrgyzstan's national epic poem, is one of the longest epic poems in the world - far longer than the Iliad and Odyssey combined.
Kyrgyzstan is sometimes called the 'Switzerland of Central Asia' because over 90% of its territory is mountainous.

tm.earliestSettlement: Ancient Merv, one of the great oasis-cities of the Silk Road, has roots going back over 2,500 years.

keyDates.event: Turkmen SSR established
Independence from the Soviet Union, October 27
UN recognizes Turkmenistan's permanent neutrality

tm.climate: Mostly arid desert (Karakum Desert covers ~70% of the country).

unesco.name: State Historical and Cultural Park 'Ancient Merv'

funFacts: Turkmenistan's Darvaza Gas Crater has been burning continuously since the 1970s.
Turkmenistan is one of the world's most sparsely populated countries relative to its land area - the Karakum Desert covers most of the country.
The Akhal-Teke, Turkmenistan's national horse breed, is famous for its metallic sheen and appears on the national emblem.

us.earliestSettlement: Indigenous peoples inhabited North America for over 15,000 years before European colonization; the earliest lasting European colony was St. Augustine, Florida (1565).

keyDates.event: Declaration of Independence
US Constitution drafted
American Civil War begins
Slavery abolished (13th Amendment)
End of World War II; US emerges as a global superpower
Apollo 11 moon landing

us.climate: Extremely varied: arctic in Alaska, tropical in Hawaii/Florida, arid in the Southwest, temperate elsewhere.
funFacts: The United States has no official national language at the federal level.
Alaska is both the westernmost and, because the Aleutian Islands cross the 180th meridian, technically the easternmost US state.
The Hoover Dam used enough concrete to pave a two-lane road from San Francisco to New York.

gb.earliestSettlement: Settlement in Britain dates back to the Paleolithic; London itself was founded by the Romans as Londinium around 43 AD.

keyDates.event: Norman Conquest of England
Magna Carta signed
Acts of Union create the Kingdom of Great Britain
Act of Union with Ireland forms the United Kingdom
WWII ends; postwar decolonization begins
UK formally leaves the European Union (Brexit)

gb.climate: Temperate maritime - mild, often cloudy and rainy.
funFacts: The United Kingdom is made up of four nations: England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
The London Underground, opened in 1863, is the oldest underground railway network in the world.
Big Ben is technically the name of the bell, not the clock tower.

ru.earliestSettlement: The Kievan Rus' state, the earliest East Slavic state, was founded around 882 AD.

keyDates.event: Founding of Kievan Rus'
Ivan IV crowned first Tsar of Russia
Russian Revolution; end of the monarchy
Soviet Union formally established
Soviet Union helps defeat Nazi Germany in WWII
Dissolution of the Soviet Union

ru.climate: Vast range from subarctic/tundra in Siberia to humid continental and subtropical in the south.
ru.nationalSport: Bandy (official); ice hockey is most popular
funFacts: Russia spans 11 time zones, more than any other country.
Lake Baikal holds about 20% of the world's unfrozen fresh surface water - more than all five North American Great Lakes combined.
The Trans-Siberian Railway is the longest railway line in the world, spanning over 9,289 km.

cn.earliestSettlement: Chinese civilization along the Yellow River dates back over 5,000 years; the Shang Dynasty (c. 1600 BC) left the earliest confirmed written records.

keyDates.event: Qin Shi Huang unifies China, becomes first emperor
Mongol-led Yuan Dynasty established
Qing Dynasty falls; Republic of China founded
People's Republic of China proclaimed
Economic reforms under Deng Xiaoping begin

cn.climate: Extremely varied: monsoon in the southeast, arid in the northwest, alpine on the Tibetan Plateau.
funFacts: The Great Wall of China is not a single continuous wall, but many walls built by different dynasties over centuries.
The Three Gorges Dam is the largest power station in the world by installed capacity.
China has one official time zone for the entire country, despite spanning a width that would normally cover five.

fr.earliestSettlement: Paris began as a Celtic settlement called Lutetia, later developed by the Romans.

keyDates.event: Treaty of Verdun creates West Francia, forerunner of France
French Revolution begins
Napoleon crowned Emperor
Liberation of Paris from Nazi occupation
Fifth Republic established

fr.climate: Mostly temperate oceanic; Mediterranean in the south.
funFacts: France is the world's most-visited country by international tourist arrivals.
The Eiffel Tower was meant to be a temporary structure for the 1889 World's Fair.
France has more time zones than any other country (12), owing to its overseas territories.

de.earliestSettlement: Germanic tribes inhabited the region from antiquity; Trier, founded by the Romans around 16 BC, claims to be Germany's oldest city.

keyDates.event: German Empire unified under Prussia
Nazi Party seizes power
End of WWII; Germany divided
Berlin Wall built
Fall of the Berlin Wall
German reunification

de.climate: Temperate seasonal, with warm summers and cold (but not extreme) winters.
funFacts: Germany has over 1,500 different types of sausage (Wurst).
The Autobahn is famous for having stretches with no general speed limit.
Germany is home to more than 20,000 castles.

jp.earliestSettlement: The Jōmon period, one of the earliest known pottery-making cultures, dates back over 14,000 years in Japan.

keyDates.event: Nara established as the first permanent capital
Tokugawa Shogunate begins, over 250 years of relative isolation
Meiji Restoration; Japan rapidly modernizes
WWII ends after atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
Tokyo hosts the first Olympics in Asia

jp.climate: Varies north to south: humid continental in Hokkaido to subtropical in Okinawa.
funFacts: Japan's Shinkansen (bullet train) began service in 1964 and has carried billions of passengers with no passenger fatalities from derailment or collision.
Japan has the world's oldest continuously operating company, Kongō Gumi, founded in 578 AD.
Japan consists of over 6,800 islands.

in.earliestSettlement: The Indus Valley Civilization, one of the world's earliest urban cultures, flourished from around 3300 BC.

keyDates.event: Indus Valley Civilization at its peak
Mughal Empire founded
British Crown rule begins
Independence and Partition, August 15
India becomes a republic

in.climate: Monsoon-dominated, ranging from tropical in the south to alpine in the Himalayas.
funFacts: India is home to the Statue of Unity, the tallest statue in the world at 182 metres.
India has 22 officially recognized languages and hundreds more spoken regionally.
The game of chess is believed to have originated in India.

government.form: Federal elective monarchy (federation of seven emirates)

ae.earliestSettlement: Archaeological sites near Al Ain show settlement dating back over 5,000 years.

keyDates.event: Perpetual Maritime Truce signed with Britain
United Arab Emirates formed, December 2
UAE dirham introduced as common currency
Burj Khalifa opens as the world's tallest building

historicalFigures.name: Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan

ae.climate: Arid desert - very hot summers, mild winters.
funFacts: The Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest structure in the world, standing at 828 metres.
The UAE is a federation of seven emirates: Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Fujairah, and Ras Al Khaimah.
Dubai International Airport is one of the busiest airports in the world for international passenger traffic.
The Palm Jumeirah is one of the largest artificial islands in the world, visible from space.

independence.from: Proclaimed as a republic following the collapse of the Ottoman Empire

tr.earliestSettlement: Göbekli Tepe in southeastern Turkey, dated to around 9500 BC, is among the oldest known temple complexes in the world.

keyDates.event: Constantinople founded as capital of the Roman/Byzantine Empire
Ottomans conquer Constantinople
Ottoman Sultanate abolished
Republic of Turkey proclaimed, October 29

tr.climate: Mediterranean on the coasts, continental in the interior.
funFacts: Istanbul is the only major city in the world that spans two continents, Europe and Asia.
Göbekli Tepe predates Stonehenge by roughly 6,000 years.
Turkey is home to Cappadocia's famous 'fairy chimney' rock formations, shaped by volcanic ash erosion.

independence.from: Unified from earlier Saudi states, not a colonial independence

sa.earliestSettlement: The Arabian Peninsula has been inhabited since prehistoric times; Mecca has been a settlement and pilgrimage site for over a thousand years before Islam.

keyDates.event: First Saudi State founded at Diriyah
Ibn Saud recaptures Riyadh, beginning modern unification
Kingdom of Saudi Arabia proclaimed, September 23
Oil discovered in commercial quantities

sa.climate: Arid desert - extremely hot summers, mild winters.
funFacts: Saudi Aramco is one of the most valuable companies in the world by market capitalization.
Mecca receives millions of Muslim pilgrims every year during the Hajj.
Saudi Arabia has no permanent rivers.

ca.independence: July 1, 1867 (Confederation, from the United Kingdom; full legislative independence via the Statute of Westminster 1931 and Canada Act 1982)
ca.earliestSettlement: Indigenous peoples inhabited the region for over 10,000 years before European contact; permanent European settlement began with Quebec City, founded by Samuel de Champlain in 1608.

keyDates.event: Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec City
Treaty of Paris cedes New France to Britain
Confederation creates the Dominion of Canada
Statute of Westminster grants legislative independence
Canada Act patriates the constitution

ca.climate: Varies widely - arctic in the north, humid continental in central/eastern regions, oceanic on the west coast.
ca.nationalAnimal: Beaver (national symbol); moose and Canada goose also prominent
ca.nationalSport: Ice hockey (lacrosse is the official summer national sport)
funFacts: Canada has the longest coastline of any country in the world.
Canada has more lakes than the rest of the world's lakes combined.
The world's first IMAX film was shown in Canada in 1970.

au.independence: January 1, 1901 (Federation of the Australian colonies; full legislative independence via the Statute of Westminster, adopted 1942)
au.earliestSettlement: Aboriginal Australians have inhabited the continent for at least 50,000-65,000 years, among the oldest continuous cultures on Earth.

keyDates.event: James Cook charts and claims the east coast for Britain
First Fleet arrives, founding the colony of New South Wales
Federation of Australia
Gallipoli campaign, formative in national identity (ANZAC)
Australia Act severs remaining legal ties to the UK Parliament

au.climate: Arid/desert across most of the interior; tropical in the north, temperate in the south and east.
au.nationalAnimal: Red kangaroo (emu also a national symbol)
au.nationalSport: Cricket (informally); Australian rules football is the most-attended
funFacts: Australia is the only country that is also a continent.
Over 80% of Australia's plants, mammals, reptiles and frogs are found nowhere else on Earth.
Australia has more venomous snake species than any other country.

br.independence: September 7, 1822, from Portugal (declared by Prince Pedro, who became Emperor Pedro I)
br.earliestSettlement: Indigenous peoples inhabited Brazil for thousands of years; Portuguese colonization began in 1500 when Pedro Alvares Cabral landed on the coast.

keyDates.event: Pedro Alvares Cabral claims Brazil for Portugal
Independence declared by Pedro I
Slavery abolished (Lei Aurea)
Monarchy abolished, republic proclaimed
Capital moved from Rio de Janeiro to newly built Brasília

br.climate: Mostly tropical; equatorial in the Amazon, semi-arid in the northeast, subtropical in the south.
majorReligions: Christianity (Roman Catholic majority, large Protestant minority)

unesco.name: Historic Centre of Salvador de Bahia

funFacts: Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in the Americas.
The Amazon River discharges more water than the next seven largest rivers combined.
Brasília was purpose-built as the capital and completed in just 41 months.

mx.independence: September 16, 1810 (start of war of independence); formally recognized September 27, 1821, from Spain
mx.earliestSettlement: Home to major pre-Columbian civilizations including the Olmec, Maya, and Aztec; Tenochtitlan, the Aztec capital, was founded around 1325 on the site of modern Mexico City.

keyDates.event: Aztecs found Tenochtitlan
Spanish conquest of the Aztec Empire under Hernan Cortes
Miguel Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores begins the independence war
Mexican-American War begins (Mexico loses roughly half its territory)
Mexican Revolution begins

mx.climate: Highly varied - arid in the north, tropical on the coasts, temperate highlands in the central plateau.
mx.nationalSport: Charreria (rodeo-style sport); football is the most popular spectator sport

unesco.name: Historic Centre of Mexico City and Xochimilco

funFacts: Mexico City was built on the site of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, itself built on a lake.
Mexico introduced chocolate, corn, tomatoes and chili peppers to the world.
Mexico has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country in the Americas.

it.independence: March 17, 1861 (Unification of Italy, Kingdom of Italy proclaimed)
it.earliestSettlement: Rome traditionally founded 753 BC; the Italian peninsula was home to Etruscan and Greek colonies even earlier.

keyDates.event: Traditional founding of Rome
Fall of the Western Roman Empire
Unification - Kingdom of Italy proclaimed
Mussolini's March on Rome, rise of Fascism
Referendum abolishes the monarchy, Republic of Italy founded

it.climate: Mediterranean along the coasts, alpine in the north.

nationalDish.name: Pasta (regionally varied; no single official dish)

funFacts: Italy has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country.
Italy is home to the world's two smallest sovereign states as enclaves: Vatican City and San Marino.
The pizza Margherita was named after Queen Margherita of Savoy in 1889.

es.earliestSettlement: Inhabited since prehistoric times (Altamira cave paintings date to c. 36,000 years ago); unified under the Catholic Monarchs in 1469-1492.

keyDates.event: Umayyad conquest begins Islamic rule (Al-Andalus)
Fall of Granada completes the Reconquista; Columbus reaches the Americas
Spanish Armada defeated by England
Spanish Civil War begins
Death of Franco, transition to democracy begins

es.climate: Mediterranean along the coasts, semi-arid in the interior, oceanic in the northwest.
es.nationalSport: Football (soccer); bullfighting is a traditional spectacle

unesco.name: Sagrada Familia and Gaudi works, Barcelona

funFacts: Spain has the second-most UNESCO World Heritage Sites of any country, after Italy.
Spain's siesta tradition arose from the need to avoid the midday heat during farm work.
The Sagrada Familia has been under construction since 1882 and is still unfinished.

eg.independence: February 28, 1922, from the United Kingdom (full sovereignty recognized progressively; 1952 revolution ended the monarchy)
formerNames: United Arab Republic (1958-1961, union with Syria)
eg.earliestSettlement: One of the world's oldest civilizations, with settled agriculture along the Nile from around 6000 BC and unification under the first pharaoh around 3100 BC.

keyDates.event: Unification of Upper and Lower Egypt under Narmer
Great Pyramid of Giza built (approx.)
Arab conquest of Egypt
Nominal independence from Britain
Revolution overthrows the monarchy

eg.climate: Desert, hot and dry; the Nile Valley and Delta are the main fertile regions.
eg.nationalSport: Football (soccer); squash also very strong internationally

unesco.name: Memphis and its Necropolis (Pyramids of Giza)

funFacts: The Great Pyramid of Giza was the tallest man-made structure in the world for almost 3,800 years.
The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, connects the Mediterranean and Red Seas, avoiding the trip around Africa.
Ancient Egyptian hieroglyphs were only deciphered after the discovery of the Rosetta Stone in 1799.

za.independence: May 31, 1910 (Union of South Africa from Britain); May 31, 1961 full republic
za.earliestSettlement: Home to some of the earliest evidence of modern humans; Dutch settlers founded Cape Town in 1652 as a Dutch East India Company supply station.

keyDates.event: Dutch found Cape Town
Union of South Africa formed
Apartheid system formally institutionalized
Nelson Mandela released from prison
First democratic multi-racial elections; Mandela becomes president

za.climate: Mostly semi-arid, Mediterranean in the southwest, subtropical on the east coast.
za.nationalSport: Rugby union (football and cricket also very popular)
funFacts: South Africa has three capital cities: Pretoria (administrative), Cape Town (legislative), Bloemfontein (judicial).
South Africa has 12 official languages, more than any other country.
Nelson Mandela spent 27 years in prison before becoming the country's first democratically elected president.

kr.independence: August 15, 1945, from Japanese colonial rule (Republic of Korea formally established August 15, 1948)
kr.earliestSettlement: Korean history traces back to ancient kingdoms such as Gojoseon; the Silla, Goguryeo and Baekje kingdoms shaped the peninsula from around the 1st century BC.

keyDates.event: Silla unifies the Three Kingdoms of Korea
Joseon Dynasty founded
Annexed by Japan
Liberation and division of Korea
Korean War begins

kr.climate: Temperate, with four distinct seasons; humid continental in the north, humid subtropical in the south.

nationalDish.name: Kimchi (as a staple; bibimbap and bulgogi also iconic)

funFacts: South Korea has one of the fastest average internet speeds in the world.
The Korean alphabet, Hangul, was deliberately designed and introduced in 1443 by King Sejong.
South Korea transformed from one of the world's poorest countries to a top-15 economy within a few decades, known as the 'Miracle on the Han River.'

id.independence: August 17, 1945, from the Netherlands (Dutch recognition came in 1949 after a war of independence)
id.earliestSettlement: The archipelago was shaped by powerful Hindu-Buddhist empires such as Srivijaya and Majapahit from around the 7th century CE onward.

keyDates.event: Majapahit Empire founded
Dutch East India Company (VOC) established, beginning colonial control
Sukarno proclaims independence
Netherlands formally recognizes Indonesian sovereignty
Suharto's 32-year authoritarian rule ends

id.climate: Tropical, hot and humid year-round; monsoonal rainfall patterns.
id.nationalSport: Badminton (unofficially, dominant on the world stage); Pencak Silat is the traditional martial art
funFacts: Indonesia is the world's largest archipelago, with over 17,000 islands.
Indonesia has more active volcanoes than any other country.
Jakarta is sinking so fast that Indonesia is building an entirely new capital city, Nusantara, on Borneo.

formerNames: United Provinces of the Rio de la Plata
ar.earliestSettlement: Indigenous peoples inhabited the region for millennia; Buenos Aires was founded by Spanish settlers in 1536 (refounded 1580).

keyDates.event: Buenos Aires first founded by Spanish settlers
Declaration of independence from Spain
Juan Peron elected president, beginning Peronism
Military coup begins the 'Dirty War' dictatorship
Return to democracy

ar.climate: Highly varied - subtropical in the north, temperate in the central Pampas, arid/cold in Patagonia.
ar.nationalAnimal: Rufous hornero (national bird); the puma is a notable symbol
ar.nationalSport: Pato (official); football is the most popular
funFacts: Argentina is home to Aconcagua, the highest peak outside Asia.
Tango originated in the working-class neighborhoods of Buenos Aires in the late 19th century.
Argentina has won the FIFA World Cup three times, most recently in 2022.

ir.earliestSettlement: One of the world's oldest continuous civilizations, with the Achaemenid Persian Empire founded by Cyrus the Great around 550 BC.

keyDates.event: Cyrus the Great founds the Achaemenid Empire
Arab-Muslim conquest ends the Sasanian Empire
Safavid dynasty establishes Shia Islam as state religion
Islamic Revolution overthrows the Shah
Iran-Iraq War begins (ends 1988)

ir.climate: Mostly arid and semi-arid, with subtropical areas along the Caspian coast.
funFacts: Iran was known as Persia to the Western world until 1935.
Persepolis was the ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire, founded by Darius I around 518 BC.
Iran has one of the oldest postal/road systems in history - the Royal Road built under the Achaemenids.

government.nationalDay: Independence Day (Hebrew calendar date, varies, April/May)

il.independence: May 14, 1948 (declared, following the end of the British Mandate for Palestine)
il.earliestSettlement: The region has continuous Jewish historical and religious ties dating back over 3,000 years; Jerusalem has been continuously inhabited for thousands of years.

keyDates.event: Balfour Declaration supports a Jewish homeland in Palestine
State of Israel declared; War of Independence follows
Six-Day War
Peace treaty with Egypt
Oslo Accords with the Palestine Liberation Organization

il.climate: Mediterranean along the coast, semi-arid to arid in the south (Negev desert).

nationalDish.name: Hummus / Falafel (widely cited, shared regional dishes)

funFacts: Israel has one of the highest numbers of startups per capita in the world, earning the nickname 'Start-Up Nation.'
Hebrew was revived as a modern spoken language in the late 19th/early 20th century after centuries as primarily a liturgical language.
The Dead Sea, bordering Israel, is the lowest point on Earth's land surface.

ng.earliestSettlement: Home to ancient civilizations including the Nok culture (c. 1500 BC) and the Benin and Oyo empires before British colonization.

keyDates.event: British merge Northern and Southern Nigeria protectorates
Independence from Britain
Biafran War begins (ends 1970)
Return to civilian democratic rule after years of military rule
Capital officially moved from Lagos to Abuja

ng.climate: Tropical, varying from equatorial in the south to semi-arid/Sahel in the far north.
ng.nationalAnimal: Eagle (featured on the coat of arms)
funFacts: Nigeria is Africa's most populous country.
Nollywood, Nigeria's film industry, is one of the largest film producers in the world by volume.
Nigeria has over 500 languages spoken within its borders.

pk.independence: August 14, 1947, from the United Kingdom (partition of British India)
pk.earliestSettlement: Home to the Indus Valley Civilization (Mohenjo-daro, c. 2500 BC), one of the world's earliest urban civilizations.

keyDates.event: Indus Valley Civilization flourishes (Mohenjo-daro)
Partition of India creates Pakistan
East Pakistan secedes to become Bangladesh
Pakistan conducts nuclear tests
First of several military coups (Ayub Khan)

pk.climate: Mostly arid/semi-arid, alpine in the mountainous north.
pk.nationalSport: Field hockey (official); cricket is the most popular
funFacts: Pakistan is home to K2, the world's second-highest mountain and one of the most dangerous to climb.
The Indus Valley Civilization, centered in modern Pakistan, had advanced urban planning and sanitation systems 4,500 years ago.
Pakistan has the second-largest Muslim population of any country, after Indonesia.

government.nationalDay: December 5 (birthday of the late King Bhumibol, observed as National Day)

th.earliestSettlement: The Sukhothai Kingdom (founded 1238) is traditionally regarded as the first Thai kingdom; the Ayutthaya Kingdom followed in 1351.

keyDates.event: Sukhothai Kingdom founded, traditional start of the Thai nation
Ayutthaya Kingdom founded
Rattanakosin era begins, Bangkok founded as capital
Revolution ends absolute monarchy, constitutional monarchy begins
Country renamed from Siam to Thailand

th.climate: Tropical, hot and humid with a monsoon season.
funFacts: Thailand is the only Southeast Asian country never colonized by a European power.
Bangkok's full ceremonial name is one of the longest place names in the world.
Thailand is the world's largest exporter of canned tuna.

vn.independence: September 2, 1945 (declared from France/Japan); formally recognized after the First Indochina War, 1954
formerNames: Democratic Republic of Vietnam / Republic of Vietnam (divided 1954-1975)
vn.earliestSettlement: Vietnamese civilization traces back to the Hong Bang dynasty (traditionally from c. 2879 BC) and the Dong Son culture of the Bronze Age.

keyDates.event: Beginning of roughly 1,000 years of Chinese rule (ends 939 AD)
Ho Chi Minh declares independence
Battle of Dien Bien Phu ends French rule; country divided at 17th parallel
Fall of Saigon, Vietnam War ends, country reunified
Doi Moi economic reforms begin

vn.climate: Tropical in the south, monsoonal with a more temperate winter in the north.
vn.nationalSport: Vo vietnam (martial art); football is the most popular spectator sport
funFacts: Vietnam is the world's second-largest coffee exporter after Brazil.
The Vietnam War is known domestically as the 'American War.'
Ha Long Bay contains around 1,600 limestone islands and islets.

pl.independence: November 11, 1918 (re-established after 123 years of partition between Russia, Prussia and Austria)
pl.earliestSettlement: The Polish state traditionally dates to 966 AD, when Duke Mieszko I converted to Christianity (the Baptism of Poland).

keyDates.event: Baptism of Poland, traditional founding of the Polish state
Union of Lublin creates the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
Third Partition erases Poland from the map for 123 years
Poland regains independence
Solidarity movement leads to the fall of communism

pl.climate: Temperate, transitional between oceanic and continental.
funFacts: Poland disappeared from the map of Europe for 123 years (1795-1918) after being partitioned by its neighbors.
Nicolaus Copernicus, Marie Curie and Frederic Chopin were all Polish.
The Wieliczka Salt Mine has been in continuous operation since the 13th century and includes entire chapels carved from salt.

nl.independence: Formally recognized 1648 (Peace of Westphalia), following the Union of Utrecht 1579
nl.earliestSettlement: Low-lying delta lands settled since prehistoric times; the Dutch Republic rose to global prominence as a major trading and colonial power in the 17th-century 'Golden Age.'

keyDates.event: Union of Utrecht, founding basis of the Dutch Republic
Peace of Westphalia formally recognizes Dutch independence from Spain
Dutch East India Company founded, world's first multinational corporation
Nazi Germany invades and occupies the Netherlands
Founding member of the European Economic Community

nl.climate: Temperate maritime, mild winters and cool summers.
nl.nationalSport: Football (soccer); speed skating and cycling culturally significant
funFacts: About a third of the Netherlands lies at or below sea level, reclaimed and protected by dikes and pumps.
The Dutch East India Company, founded in 1602, is considered the world's first publicly traded company.
The Netherlands is the world's second-largest exporter of food by value, despite its small size.

gr.independence: Independence declared March 25, 1821, from the Ottoman Empire (recognized 1830)
gr.earliestSettlement: Birthplace of Western civilization; Minoan and Mycenaean civilizations flourished from around 3000-1100 BC, followed by Classical Greece.

keyDates.event: Traditional date of the first Olympic Games
Athenian democracy established under Cleisthenes
Fall of Constantinople ends the Byzantine Empire
Greek War of Independence begins

gr.climate: Mediterranean, hot dry summers and mild wet winters.

Herero and Namaqua genocide begins under German colonial rule
South Africa takes over administration under a League of Nations mandate
Namibian War of Independence begins
Independence from South Africa

na.climate: Arid to semi-arid; the Namib is one of the world's oldest and driest deserts.
funFacts: The Namib Desert, after which the country is named, is considered one of the oldest deserts in the world.
Namibia was the first country in the world to incorporate environmental protection into its constitution.
Namibia has one of the lowest population densities of any country on Earth.

mw.earliestSettlement: Bantu-speaking peoples settled the region centuries ago, forming the Maravi Confederacy, from which the country's name derives, before British colonization as Nyasaland.

keyDates.event: Maravi Confederacy rises to prominence (approx.)
Britain establishes the Nyasaland protectorate
Independence as Malawi under Hastings Banda
Transition to multi-party democracy after 30 years of one-party rule

mw.climate: Tropical/subtropical, moderated by the Rift Valley lake.
funFacts: Malawi is nicknamed 'The Warm Heart of Africa' for the hospitality of its people.
Lake Malawi contains more fish species than any other lake in the world, including hundreds of unique cichlid species.
Malawi is one of the most densely populated countries in Africa despite being relatively small.

rw.earliestSettlement: Home to a centuries-old Tutsi-led kingdom before German and then Belgian colonization, which hardened ethnic divisions that later contributed to immense tragedy.

keyDates.event: Kingdom of Rwanda consolidates under Tutsi monarchy (approx.)
Belgium takes over administration from Germany
Independence from Belgium
Genocide against the Tutsi kills an estimated 800,000+ people in 100 days
Paul Kagame becomes president, leads major post-genocide reconstruction

rw.climate: Temperate tropical highland, moderated by altitude year-round.
funFacts: Rwanda is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Hills' for its mountainous terrain.
Since the 1994 genocide, Rwanda has rebuilt itself into one of Africa's cleanest, safest and fastest-reforming countries, including a ban on single-use plastic bags since 2008.
Rwanda has one of the highest proportions of women in parliament of any country in the world.

mn.independence: December 29, 1911 (from the Qing dynasty, autonomy); full independence recognized 1921, confirmed 1945
mn.earliestSettlement: Home to nomadic steppe peoples for millennia; Genghis Khan unified the Mongol tribes in 1206, founding the largest contiguous land empire in history.

keyDates.event: Genghis Khan unifies the Mongol tribes, founds the Mongol Empire
Kublai Khan completes the conquest of China, founds the Yuan dynasty
Mongolia comes under Qing Chinese rule
Independence with Soviet backing
Peaceful democratic revolution ends communist one-party rule

mn.climate: Extreme continental, very cold winters, warm summers; among the world's least densely populated countries.
mn.nationalSport: Wrestling (Mongolian wrestling, part of the 'Three Manly Games' with archery and horse racing)
funFacts: At its peak, the Mongol Empire founded by Genghis Khan was the largest contiguous land empire in history.
Mongolia is one of the least densely populated countries on Earth, with vast open steppe still used for nomadic herding.
Ulaanbaatar is the coldest national capital city in the world by average annual temperature.

np.independence: Never formally colonized; unified as a modern state in 1768-1769
np.earliestSettlement: The Kathmandu Valley has been continuously settled for over 2,000 years; Nepal is the birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha), born in Lumbini around the 6th century BC.

keyDates.event: Siddhartha Gautama (the Buddha) born in Lumbini (approx.)
Prithvi Narayan Shah unifies Nepal, conquering Kathmandu Valley
Treaty of Sugauli sets Nepal's modern borders after war with British India
Maoist insurgency begins (ends 2006)
Monarchy abolished, Nepal becomes a federal democratic republic

np.climate: Highly varied by altitude - subtropical lowlands (Terai) to alpine/arctic high Himalaya.
np.nationalAnimal: Cow (sacred); the Himalayan monal is the national bird
np.nationalSport: Volleyball (official); dandi biyo is a traditional sport

unesco.name: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha

funFacts: Nepal is home to eight of the world's ten highest mountains, including Mount Everest.
Nepal was never colonized by a European power.
Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that is not a rectangle or square - it's made of two overlapping triangular pennants.

bd.independence: March 26, 1971, from Pakistan (secured after a nine-month war, with Indian intervention)
bd.earliestSettlement: The Bengal region has a civilizational history stretching back thousands of years, with the ancient Pundra and Gangaridai kingdoms among the earliest recorded states.

keyDates.event: Muslim conquest of Bengal begins
Battle of Plassey - British East India Company gains control of Bengal
Partition of India creates East Pakistan
Bangladesh Liberation War secures independence from Pakistan
Return to parliamentary democracy

bd.climate: Tropical monsoon, hot and humid with a pronounced wet season and frequent cyclones.
bd.nationalSport: Kabaddi (official); cricket is the most popular spectator sport
funFacts: The Sundarbans, shared with India, is the largest mangrove forest in the world and home to the Bengal tiger.
Bangladesh has one of the highest population densities of any sizable country in the world.
Bangladesh is a world leader in ready-made garment exports, second only to China.

lk.earliestSettlement: Anuradhapura, founded around the 4th century BC, became the capital of one of the longest-lasting continuous monarchies in the world, lasting over 1,300 years.

keyDates.event: Kingdom of Anuradhapura founded (approx.)
Portuguese arrive, beginning centuries of European colonial presence
British conquer the Kingdom of Kandy, completing colonization
Independence from Britain as Ceylon
Civil war begins between the government and Tamil Tigers (ends 2009)

lk.climate: Tropical, with distinct monsoon seasons; cooler in the central highlands.
lk.nationalSport: Volleyball (official); cricket is the most popular spectator sport
funFacts: Sri Lanka was the first country in the world to elect a woman as head of government, Sirimavo Bandaranaike, in 1960.
Sigiriya, an ancient rock fortress, features frescoes and engineering dating back to the 5th century AD.
Sri Lanka is one of the world's leading tea-exporting countries, famous for 'Ceylon tea.'

government.form: Unitary military-led state (de facto, following 2021 coup)

mm.earliestSettlement: The Pyu city-states flourished from around the 2nd century BC; the Bagan Kingdom, founded in the 9th century, unified much of the region and built thousands of Buddhist temples.

keyDates.event: Bagan Kingdom founded, begins construction of thousands of temples
First Anglo-Burmese War begins, leading to eventual British colonization
Independence from Britain as Burma
Military coup begins decades of military rule
Military coup ousts the civilian government, ongoing conflict follows

mm.climate: Tropical monsoon, hot and humid with a pronounced wet season.
funFacts: Bagan contains over 2,000 surviving Buddhist temples and pagodas from its medieval golden age, one of the richest archaeological sites in Southeast Asia.
Myanmar is one of the world's leading sources of jade and rubies.
Myanmar has had two official names in recent history - Burma and Myanmar - a change adopted by the military government in 1989 that remains politically contested.

kh.earliestSettlement: The Khmer Empire, centered at Angkor, dominated Southeast Asia from the 9th-15th centuries, building the vast temple complex of Angkor Wat.

keyDates.event: Khmer Empire founded, capital established at Angkor
Construction of Angkor Wat begins under Suryavarman II
Independence from France
Khmer Rouge seizes power, begins genocide killing roughly 1.5-2 million people
Paris Peace Accords end decades of conflict

kh.climate: Tropical monsoon, hot and humid with a wet and dry season.
funFacts: Angkor Wat is the largest religious monument in the world by land area.
The Khmer Rouge regime (1975-1979) killed an estimated quarter of Cambodia's population in one of the 20th century's worst genocides.
Cambodia's flag is one of the only national flags in the world to feature a building - Angkor Wat.

la.earliestSettlement: The Kingdom of Lan Xang ('Million Elephants'), founded in 1353, was one of the largest states in Southeast Asian history, centered on the Mekong River.

keyDates.event: Kingdom of Lan Xang founded by Fa Ngum
Laos becomes a French protectorate
Full independence from France
Laos becomes heavily bombed during the Vietnam War-era Secret War
Communist Pathet Lao takes power, monarchy abolished

la.climate: Tropical monsoon, hot and humid with a wet and dry season.
la.nationalSport: Petanque (brought by the French, hugely popular); football also widely followed

unesco.name: Vat Phou and Associated Ancient Settlements

funFacts: Laos is the most heavily bombed country per capita in history, from the US 'Secret War' during the Vietnam War era.
Laos is the only landlocked country in Southeast Asia.
The mysterious Plain of Jars features thousands of massive stone jars dating back over 2,000 years, whose purpose remains debated.

bn.earliestSettlement: The Bruneian Empire, at its height in the 15th-16th centuries, controlled much of Borneo and the Philippines; the Sultanate has ruled continuously for over 600 years.

keyDates.event: Sultanate of Brunei founded
Brunei at the height of its regional power, visited by Magellan's expedition
Brunei becomes a British protectorate
Oil discovered, transforming the sultanate's economy
Full independence from Britain

bn.climate: Tropical rainforest, hot and humid year-round.

Brunei's oil and gas wealth gives it one of the highest GDP per capita figures in Asia, with no personal income tax.
The Sultanate of Brunei once controlled most of the island of Borneo and parts of the Philippines at its 16th-century peak.

bt.independence: Never formally colonized; British influence over foreign affairs ended with a 1949 treaty
formerNames: Druk Yul (native name, 'Land of the Thunder Dragon')

Wangchuck dynasty founded, hereditary monarchy begins
Bhutan joins the United Nations
Bhutan transitions to a constitutional democracy

highestPeak.name: Gangkhar Puensum (unclimbed, one of the highest unclimbed mountains in the world)

funFacts: Bhutan famously measures national progress through Gross National Happiness rather than GDP alone.
Gangkhar Puensum, Bhutan's highest peak, is one of the highest mountains in the world never to have been climbed, as mountaineering above a certain altitude is banned for religious reasons.
Bhutan is one of the only carbon-negative countries in the world, absorbing more carbon than it emits.

mv.earliestSettlement: Settled by seafaring peoples from South Asia over 2,500 years ago; converted from Buddhism to Islam in 1153, a defining event still central to national identity.

Portuguese briefly occupy Male

Independence from Britain
Sultanate abolished, republic established

highestPeak.name: Unnamed point on Villingili Island, Addu Atoll (lowest-lying country in the world)

funFacts: The Maldives is the lowest-lying country in the world, with an average elevation of just about 1.5 meters above sea level.
The Maldives is made up of around 1,192 coral islands grouped into 26 atolls.
Rising sea levels pose an existential threat to the Maldives, prompting the government to explore relocation options for its population.

formerNames: Territory of Papua and New Guinea
pg.earliestSettlement: Human settlement dates back at least 40,000-60,000 years, with highland peoples independently developing agriculture among the earliest in the world, around 7,000-10,000 years ago.

Germany and Britain divide the eastern half of New Guinea between them
Fierce WWII Pacific campaign fighting (e.g. Kokoda Track) takes place

Papua New Guinea shares its island with Indonesia, one of the few places in the world where a single island is divided between two very different countries.

fj.earliestSettlement: Settled by Austronesian and Melanesian voyagers roughly 3,500 years ago; became a British crown colony in 1874 after a period of unification under local chiefs.

Independence from Britain

Return to parliamentary democracy after the 2006 coup

fj.climate: Tropical maritime, warm year-round with a wet and dry season.

Fiji is home to a significant population of Indo-Fijians, descendants of indentured laborers brought by the British in the late 19th century.

sb.climate: Tropical rainforest, hot and humid year-round.

The Solomon Islands consist of nearly 1,000 islands spread across a vast ocean area.
The islands were named 'Solomon' by a Spanish explorer who mistakenly believed he had found the biblical King Solomon's gold mines.

vu.independence: July 30, 1980, from France and the United Kingdom (jointly, the unusual Anglo-French Condominium)

keyDates.event: Captain James Cook names the islands the New Hebrides
Britain and France establish a joint Anglo-French Condominium
Independence as Vanuatu, ending the unique dual-colonial arrangement
Cyclone Pam devastates the country

vu.climate: Tropical, warm and humid with a cyclone season.
funFacts: Vanuatu was governed under a unique joint British-French 'condominium,' a rare arrangement of two colonial powers ruling the same territory simultaneously.

Vanuatu is famous for its traditional land diving ritual on Pentecost Island, a precursor to modern bungee jumping.

Samoa divided between Germany (west) and the US (east, American Samoa)
New Zealand occupies German Samoa during WWI

ws.climate: Tropical, warm and humid year-round with a wet and dry season.

Samoa's traditional fa'a Samoa ('the Samoan way') social and chiefly system remains central to daily life and governance.

formerNames: Friendly Islands (name given by Captain Cook)

Captain Cook visits and nicknames Tonga 'the Friendly Islands'
Tonga becomes a British-protected state (retaining internal self-rule)

to.climate: Tropical, warm and humid with a cyclone season.

funFacts: Tonga is the only Pacific island nation never formally colonized by a foreign power.

Tonga's monarchy traces its line back over a thousand years, among the oldest continuous monarchies in the world.

ki.earliestSettlement: Settled by Micronesian and later Polynesian voyagers around 3,000 years ago, spread across a vast area of the central Pacific.

ki.nationalSport: Te ano (traditional ball game); football also played

Kiribati is one of the countries most threatened by rising sea levels, with its highest point only around 81 meters above sea level.

tv.earliestSettlement: Settled by Polynesian voyagers many centuries ago; administered jointly with the Gilbert Islands until separating in 1975-1978.

Tuvalu earns significant national revenue by licensing its '.tv' internet domain to streaming and media companies worldwide.
Tuvalu's highest point is less than 5 meters above sea level, making it one of the countries most vulnerable to climate change.

nr.independence: January 31, 1968, from Australia, New Zealand and the UK (jointly, as a UN trust territory)

nr.nationalSport: Australian rules football (uniquely popular for a non-Australian nation); weightlifting also notable
funFacts: Nauru is the smallest island nation in the world and the third-smallest country overall by area.

Nauru has no official capital city - government functions are centered in the Yaren district.

Second Nagorno-Karabakh War, Azerbaijan regains significant territory

Azerbaijan is home to mud volcanoes, a rare geological phenomenon found in concentrated numbers nowhere else on Earth.

Mesrop Mashtots invents the unique Armenian alphabet

famousFeature.name: Lake Sevan / Mount Ararat (visible from Armenia, located in Turkey)

Yerevan is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world, older than Rome.

The Georgian language has its own unique alphabet, unrelated to Latin, Cyrillic or Greek scripts.
Soviet leader Joseph Stalin was born in Gori, Georgia.

pa.independence: November 28, 1821, from Spain; November 3, 1903, from Colombia

Panama is a major hub for international banking and shipping, with one of the world's largest ship registries.

cr.earliestSettlement: Indigenous peoples inhabited the region for millennia before Spanish arrival; developed differently from neighboring colonies due to a lack of major mineral wealth, fostering a more egalitarian smallholder society.

gt.earliestSettlement: The heartland of the ancient Maya civilization, with great cities like Tikal flourishing from around 600 BC to 900 AD before mysterious decline.
